questions.prompt: State the magnetic flux through a flat surface in a uniform magnetic field.
questions.answer:
The magnetic flux is
\[
\Phi_B=BA\cos\theta
\]
where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec B\) and the area vector.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
questions.answer:
The SI unit is the weber:
\[
1\,\mathrm{Wb}=1\,\mathrm{T\,m^2}
\]

questions.prompt: What direction is the area vector for a flat surface?
questions.answer: The area vector is perpendicular, or normal, to the surface. Its sign depends on which side is chosen as positive.

questions.prompt: A \(0.30\,\mathrm{m^2}\) loop is perpendicular to a \(0.40\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Find the flux.
questions.answer:
Perpendicular loop means the area vector is parallel to the field:
\[
\Phi_B=BA=(0.40)(0.30)=0.12\,\mathrm{Wb}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(0.50\,\mathrm{m^2}\) loop has area vector at \(60^\circ\) to a \(0.20\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Find the flux.
When is magnetic flux through a flat loop zero?
questions.answer: For a uniform field, \(\Phi_B=BA\cos\theta\). The flux is zero when the area vector is perpendicular to the field, so the field lies in the plane of the loop.

questions.prompt: A loop has area \(0.25\,\mathrm{m^2}\) and flux \(0.10\,\mathrm{Wb}\) when perpendicular to the field. Find \(B\).
questions.answer:
For perpendicular orientation,
\[
\Phi_B=BA
\]
so
\[
B=\frac{0.10}{0.25}=0.40\,\mathrm{T}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(0.10\,\mathrm{m^2}\) coil in a \(0.80\,\mathrm{T}\) field has flux \(0.040\,\mathrm{Wb}\). Find the angle between \(\vec B\) and the area vector.
questions.answer:
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{\Phi_B}{BA}=\frac{0.040}{(0.80)(0.10)}=0.50
\]
Thus
\[
\theta=60^\circ
\]

questions.prompt: What is the net magnetic flux through any closed surface?
questions.answer:
It is zero:
\[
\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec A=0
\]
This is Gauss's law for magnetism.

questions.prompt: Why does the net magnetic flux through a closed surface vanish?
questions.answer: Magnetic field lines form closed loops rather than starting or ending on isolated magnetic charges. Any field line entering a closed surface must also leave it, so the signed net flux is zero.

questions.prompt: A flat loop is rotated from maximum positive flux to maximum negative flux in the same uniform field. What is the change in flux?
questions.answer:
Maximum positive flux is \(+BA\). Maximum negative flux is \(-BA\). The change is
\[
\Delta\Phi_B=-BA-(+BA)=-2BA
\]
The magnitude of the change is \(2BA\).

questions.prompt: A surface is parallel to the magnetic field lines. Is the flux through that surface maximum or zero?
questions.answer: It is zero. If the field lies in the plane of the surface, then the field is perpendicular to the area vector, so \(\vec B\cdot\vec A=0\).

questions.prompt: A square loop has side \(0.20\,\mathrm{m}\) in a \(0.50\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Its area vector is \(37^\circ\) from the field. Find \(\Phi_B\).
A coil has \(N\) identical turns. What is the flux linkage for uniform flux \(\Phi_B\) through each turn?
questions.answer:
The flux linkage is
\[
N\Phi_B
\]
It counts the magnetic flux through all turns of the coil.

questions.prompt: Why can magnetic flux be negative even though field strength and area are positive?
questions.answer:
Flux is a dot product:
\[
\Phi_B=\vec B\cdot\vec A=BA\cos\theta
\]
If the chosen area vector points more than \(90^\circ\) from \(\vec B\), then \(\cos\theta\) is negative.

questions.prompt: A closed surface encloses a bar magnet. What is the net magnetic flux through the surface?
questions.answer:
The net flux is zero:
\[
\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec A=0
\]
The magnet has north and south poles, but no isolated magnetic charge is enclosed.

questions.prompt: A magnetic field is nonuniform over a surface. Why is \(BA\cos\theta\) not generally enough?
questions.answer:
The field magnitude or direction changes over the surface, so one value of \(B\) and one angle cannot represent the whole surface. Use the flux integral:
\[
\Phi_B=\int\vec B\cdot d\vec A
\]

questions.prompt: Two surfaces have the same area in the same uniform field. One has twice the flux of the other. What can you infer about their orientations?
questions.answer:
Since \(\Phi_B=BA\cos\theta\) and \(B\) and \(A\) are the same, the cosines of their angles differ by a factor of two:
\[
\cos\theta_1=2\cos\theta_2
\]
The surface with larger flux has its area vector closer to the field direction.

questions.prompt: Explain why changing only the sign convention for the area vector changes the sign of flux but not the physical field.
questions.answer: The area vector is a chosen normal direction. Reversing it sends \(\vec A\rightarrow-\vec A\), so \(\Phi_B=\vec B\cdot\vec A\) changes sign. The magnetic field itself is unchanged; only the positive-flux convention changed.

questions.prompt: Use magnetic flux to state the difference between a magnetic field with no monopoles and an electric field with enclosed charge.
questions.answer:
For magnetism, every closed surface has zero net flux:
\[
\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec A=0
\]
For electricity, a closed surface can have nonzero net electric flux when it encloses net charge:
\[
\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec A=\frac{Q_{\mathrm{enc}}}{\epsilon_0}
\]
The difference reflects the absence of isolated magnetic charge in ordinary electromagnetism.
